policy: A source is educational context. An expert view is dated opinion. Neither changes indicators, execution, risk, model weights, orders or promotion without measured validation.

sources.title: Trading and Exchanges: Market Microstructure for Practitioners
sources.lesson: Orders, liquidity provision and trading costs belong in the same execution analysis.
sources.research_translation: Add quote, auction and broker-fill data before validating an execution policy.

sources.title: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sources.lesson: Trend, chart and intermarket methods provide explicit candidate descriptions; each still needs a cost-aware test.
sources.research_translation: Expose each indicator and its conflicts; do not assume a chart label predicts returns.

sources.title: Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale
sources.lesson: Mean reversion and momentum are different strategy families with implementation assumptions.
sources.research_translation: Specify a rationale, holding horizon and executable return before testing one family.

sources.title: Evidence-Based Technical Analysis
sources.lesson: Objective, falsifiable rules and statistical inference are necessary for evaluating technical claims.
sources.research_translation: Freeze a single rule and preserve rejected results instead of selecting charts after the outcome.

sources.title: Advances in Financial Machine Learning
sources.lesson: Financial data and dependent labels require finance-specific model validation.
sources.research_translation: Version labels and inputs; separate model selection from genuinely unseen confirmation.

sources.title: Adaptive Markets: Financial Evolution at the Speed of Thought
sources.lesson: Market behavior can change as participants and environments change.
sources.research_translation: Treat regime conditioning as a separately frozen hypothesis with enough observations per regime.

sources.title: Active Portfolio Management, Second Edition
sources.authors: Richard C. Grinold and Ronald N. Kahn
sources.lesson: Benchmark-relative performance, residual risk and turnover belong in portfolio evaluation.
sources.research_translation: Measure correlated exposure and costs rather than adding independent single-name backtests.

sources.title: Expectations Investing: Reading Stock Prices for Better Returns, Revised and Updated
sources.authors: Michael J. Mauboussin and Alfred Rappaport
sources.lesson: Stock prices can be analyzed through the future business expectations they imply.
sources.research_translation: Require timestamped filings and contemporaneous expectations before constructing valuation features.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov and Sasha Stoikov
sources.lesson: In the studied US stocks, short-horizon price changes relate to order-flow imbalance and depth.
sources.research_translation: Requires actual order-book events; daily volume is not a replacement for order-flow imbalance.

sources.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado and Qiji Jim Zhu
sources.lesson: Selection across backtests can produce unreliable apparent out-of-sample winners.
sources.research_translation: Record all attempted specifications and keep future confirmation untouched; no search on these diagnostics.

sources.title: Fact, Fiction and Momentum Investing
sources.authors: Cliff Asness, Andrea Frazzini, Ronen Israel and Tobias Moskowitz
sources.lesson: Momentum research addresses a specified strategy and horizon, not every momentum oscillator.
sources.research_translation: Distinguish intermediate-horizon cross-sectional momentum from the bot's short-term RSI or SMA conditions.

sources.title: Sea Change
sources.lesson: The memo argues that a changed rate environment can alter investment opportunity and risk.
sources.research_translation: Store as dated expert opinion; never convert the author's authority into a numeric buy/sell input.

sources.title: Valuation Online and Accounting Resources
sources.lesson: Accounting and valuation require structured interpretation of financial statements.
sources.research_translation: Add filing-availability timestamps, accounting definitions and revision handling before valuation signals.

sources.title: NYSE Holidays and Trading Hours
sources.lesson: NYSE sessions include holidays and early closes.
sources.research_translation: Use a versioned exchange calendar; calendar-day or 24/7 assumptions are not valid stock session rules.

sources.title: NYSE Trading Information: LULD and Market-Wide Circuit Breakers
sources.lesson: Price bands and trading halts can interrupt ordinary order execution.
sources.research_translation: Collect timestamped halt and band states; missing state must not be inferred from a price bar.

sources.title: Shortening the Securities Transaction Settlement Cycle
sources.lesson: Most covered securities transactions have a standard one-business-day settlement cycle.
sources.research_translation: Reconcile available cash and settlement dates with the broker before allowing a cash-account order.

sources.title: Technical Analysis Explained, Fifth Edition
sources.lesson: Trend and momentum indicators provide a vocabulary for price behavior.
sources.research_translation: Specify objective rules and holdouts before testing any chart interpretation.

sources.title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques
sources.lesson: Candlestick descriptions organize open-high-low-close observations.
sources.research_translation: Define patterns numerically and evaluate incremental value after costs.

sources.title: Bollinger on Bollinger Bands
sources.lesson: Volatility bands describe prices relative to a changing distribution.
sources.research_translation: Treat a band touch as context until a regime-specific hypothesis passes validation.

sources.title: The New Trading for a Living
sources.lesson: Trading tools, discipline, risk control and trade management are connected.
sources.research_translation: Record a pre-trade plan and test exits as rigorously as entries.

sources.title: Trading Systems and Methods, Sixth Edition
sources.lesson: Trading-system design encompasses many competing methods and assumptions.
sources.research_translation: Catalog families without sweeping them against the same confirmation sample.

sources.title: Quantitative Trading: How to Build Your Own Algorithmic Trading Business, Revised Second Edition
sources.lesson: Quantitative trading combines strategy design with a reproducible operating process.
sources.research_translation: Require a data, implementation, costs and operational evidence package for each hypothesis.

sources.title: Machine Trading: Deploying Computer Algorithms to Conquer the Markets
sources.lesson: Automated strategies need deployment and testing discipline.
sources.research_translation: Connect model output to a versioned, reconciled execution contract.

sources.title: Expected Returns: An Investor's Guide to Harvesting Market Rewards
sources.lesson: Return expectations depend on risk exposures, strategies and economic conditions.
sources.research_translation: Separate risk-premium exposure from incremental stock-selection skill.

sources.title: Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading
sources.authors: Alvaro Cartea, Sebastian Jaimungal and Jose Penalva
sources.lesson: Execution and market making require models tied to market mechanics.
sources.research_translation: Require order-level data and fill assumptions before using an execution model.

sources.title: Market Microstructure Theory
sources.lesson: Market microstructure theory studies how trading arrangements affect prices and liquidity.
sources.research_translation: Distinguish information, inventory and transaction-cost hypotheses in execution research.

sources.title: Security Analysis, Seventh Edition
sources.lesson: Security analysis connects financial statements, valuation and downside considerations.
sources.research_translation: Use contemporaneously available fundamentals instead of present-day restated snapshots.

sources.title: The Intelligent Investor, Updated Edition
sources.authors: Benjamin Graham; updated commentary by Jason Zweig
sources.lesson: The book's value-investing framework emphasizes analytical discipline and long-horizon decisions.
sources.research_translation: Keep valuation hypotheses separate from short-horizon technical timing rules.

sources.title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits and Other Writings
sources.lesson: Business quality and growth analysis provide a distinct approach to equity selection.
sources.research_translation: Translate qualitative claims into timestamped financial or operational measurements before testing.

sources.title: Investment Valuation, Fourth Edition
sources.lesson: Valuation models make assumptions about cash flows, growth and risk explicit.
sources.research_translation: Preserve assumption versions and the publication dates of every input.

sources.title: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies, Eighth Edition
sources.authors: Tim Koller, Marc Goedhart and David Wessels
sources.lesson: Company value analysis connects operating performance, investment and financial expectations.
sources.research_translation: Audit accounting definitions and use sensitivity analysis without optimizing trading outcomes.

sources.title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
sources.lesson: Market efficiency and low-cost benchmark perspectives challenge claims of easy active outperformance.
sources.research_translation: Require evidence of net incremental value relative to a suitable benchmark.

sources.title: The Four Pillars of Investing, Second Edition
sources.lesson: Investment theory, history, psychology and business costs shape portfolio outcomes.
sources.research_translation: Review concentration, costs and benchmark risk before accepting apparent strategy skill.

sources.title: Against the Gods: The Remarkable Story of Risk
sources.lesson: The history of risk measurement provides perspective on probabilistic decisions.
sources.research_translation: Report uncertainty and tail scenarios rather than treating a point estimate as certainty.

sources.title: Fooled by Randomness
sources.lesson: Observed success can mix luck, selection and genuine skill.
sources.research_translation: Preserve failed experiments and demand enough independent future outcomes.

sources.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
sources.lesson: Judgment and intuition can be affected by systematic biases.
sources.research_translation: Use a reproducible decision journal and precommitted rules; this is process guidance, not trading alpha.

sources.title: Trading in the Zone
sources.lesson: Trader consistency is a process and behavioral concern.
sources.research_translation: Translate process discipline into bounded controls and reviewable actions rather than claims about a bot's emotions.

sources.title: The Daily Trading Coach
sources.lesson: Structured self-review can distinguish repeatable process from reactive decisions.
sources.research_translation: Use measured post-run attribution and document falsification before starting another experiment.

sources.title: Market Wizards: Interviews with Top Traders, Updated
sources.lesson: Trader interviews present diverse practices and experiences.
sources.research_translation: Label interviews as practitioner accounts; do not infer a replicable edge from reputation or anecdotes.

sources.title: Technical Analysis: The Complete Resource for Financial Market Technicians, Third Edition
sources.authors: Charles D. Kirkpatrick II and Julie R. Dahlquist
sources.lesson: Technical methods can be organized alongside evidence for and against their use.
sources.research_translation: Maintain both a hypothesis and its strongest counterargument for each indicator.

sources.title: The Psychology of Money
sources.lesson: Financial decisions involve behavior and uncertainty as well as calculations.
sources.research_translation: Use bounded capital, documented objectives and explicit uncertainty; this does not create a return signal.

catalog_status: Initial expanding curriculum; source records and original lesson notes are not full-text ingestion or model training.
